performers: The Mannes-Gimpel-Silva Trio: Leopold Mannes, piano; Bronislav Gimpel, violin; Luigi Silva, cello
intro: The first movement, Allegro moderato, of Clara Schumann’s Piano Trio in G minor, Op. 17, draws on a falling fifth in the violin as the source of material shared by all three players. Schumann set the second theme in B♭ major and brought it back in G major, and the movement closes in G minor.

sections.label: A · Falling fifth in the violin
B · Piano theme in B♭ major
B′ · Piano theme in G major

cues.title: First subject, violin
cues.text: The violin’s melody falls from D to G, then climbs to E♭. Beneath it the piano plays rocking quavers. When the piano takes up the tune, violin and cello add answering lines.
cues.evidence: Clara Schumann, Piano Trio, first edition (Breitkopf & Härtel, plate 7562), printed p. 2, bars 1–15. Pearson’s set-work guide identifies the first subject and its transfer from violin to piano: https://qualifications.pearson.com/content/dam/pdf/A%20Level/Music/2016/teaching-and-learning-materials/A_level_Schumann_Piano_Trio_set_work_support_guide.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Second subject in B♭ major
cues.text: The second theme is in B♭ major. The piano holds long notes across the beat, then breaks into quick repeated figures. Violin and cello follow with rising phrases built on diminished sevenths.
cues.evidence: First edition, printed p. 4, bars 45–69. Pearson’s guide, pp. 3 and 6, describes the syncopated second subject and the strings’ rising diminished-seventh figures. https://qualifications.pearson.com/content/dam/pdf/A%20Level/Music/2016/teaching-and-learning-materials/A_level_Schumann_Piano_Trio_set_work_support_guide.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Development section
cues.text: In the development, fragments of the opening melody pass between cello and violin. The falling fifth widens or narrows as the harmony changes. Beneath the strings, the piano moves from descending chords to rapid arpeggios.
cues.evidence: First edition, printed pp. 5–8, bars 91–164. Pearson’s guide, pp. 3–5, traces the altered opening intervals, imitative string entries and piano arpeggios. https://qualifications.pearson.com/content/dam/pdf/A%20Level/Music/2016/teaching-and-learning-materials/A_level_Schumann_Piano_Trio_set_work_support_guide.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Recapitulation, first subject
cues.text: The violin plays its opening melody again in G minor over the piano’s rocking quavers. After the close exchanges of the development, the original phrase returns with little change.
cues.evidence: First edition, printed pp. 8–9; recapitulation from bar 165. Pearson’s guide identifies bars 165–190 as a verbatim return of the first-subject group. https://qualifications.pearson.com/content/dam/pdf/A%20Level/Music/2016/teaching-and-learning-materials/A_level_Schumann_Piano_Trio_set_work_support_guide.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Second subject in G major
cues.text: The piano’s second theme returns at bar 210 in G major, the tonic major. Clara keeps its offbeat long notes and quick replies. From bar 220 the music moves briefly towards B major, a key remote from the two flats of the opening.
cues.evidence: First edition, printed pp. 10–11. Pearson’s guide, p. 4, places the second subject in G major from bar 210 and its excursion towards B major from bar 220. https://qualifications.pearson.com/content/dam/pdf/A%20Level/Music/2016/teaching-and-learning-materials/A_level_Schumann_Piano_Trio_set_work_support_guide.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Coda in G minor
cues.text: The coda is in G minor. The opening melody returns in violin and cello, then breaks into shorter exchanged figures. A held G in the bass sustains the final chain of cadences.
cues.evidence: First edition, printed pp. 12–13; G minor from bar 250, the first theme from bar 266, and tonic pedal from bar 276. Pearson’s guide, pp. 4–5: https://qualifications.pearson.com/content/dam/pdf/A%20Level/Music/2016/teaching-and-learning-materials/A_level_Schumann_Piano_Trio_set_work_support_guide.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

composer.epithet: Performer on the concert platform for forty years, who wrote of making music, ‘It is the air I breathe.’
facts: Piano with her father Friedrich Wieck; private lessons in composition and languages
Leipzig début, 1828; last public concert, Frankfurt, 1891
A piano concerto, a piano trio, songs, romances and variations
composer.background:
On 9 November 1835 the sixteen-year-old Clara Wieck played her A minor Piano Concerto at the Leipzig Gewandhaus, with Mendelssohn conducting. In the middle movement the orchestra stops. The piano begins a Romance in A♭ major, and a solo cello joins it, so that for a few minutes the concerto is a duet. That evening Clara also played Mendelssohn’s Capriccio brillant, and with him and Louis Rakemann she played Bach’s Concerto for Three Keyboards.

She was born in Leipzig on 13 September 1819. Her mother, Mariane, was a pianist and singer; her father, Friedrich Wieck, taught piano and sold instruments. After their divorce in 1825, Clara remained with him. He arranged lessons in harmony, counterpoint and languages, supervised her practising and required daily walks. Private teachers supplied most of her education. He also managed her concert tours.
